question: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

CCP General Secretary Xi Jinping will be considered removed from power if he announces his resignation from his role as General Secretary, or is otherwise dismissed, detained, disqualified, or otherwise loses his position or is prevented from fulfilling his duties as General Secretary within this market's timeframe.

The primary resolution source for this market will be a consensus of credible reporting.

events.title: Xi Jinping out before 2027?
events.description:
This market will resolve to "Yes" if China's General Secretary of the Communist Party, Xi Jinping, is removed from power for any length of time between July 3, 2025, and December 31, 2026, 11:59 PM ET. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

eventMetadata.context_description: Xi Jinping’s firm grip on the Chinese Communist Party apparatus, Central Military Commission, and security organs—bolstered by repeated high-level purges and appointment of loyalists—underpins the near-certain trader consensus that he will retain power through the end of 2026. With no institutional leadership transition scheduled before the 21st Party Congress in late 2027 and presidential term limits eliminated since 2018, recent months have shown continued public appearances, policy addresses, and personnel moves that reinforce policy continuity rather than any shift. The 21st Congress is widely expected to deliver Xi a fourth term, deferring succession questions. While low-probability tail risks such as a sudden health event, coordinated elite challenge, or acute economic or geopolitical crisis could theoretically alter the timeline, no credible reporting or developments currently point to such an outcome before the market resolves.
